evidence.detail: Repository HEAD exactly matches the launcher-supplied target commit.
ROADMAP.md exists and identifies roadmap v6 as DRAFT pending review and human approval.
Reviewed the approved brief, roadmap, proposed ISSUE-0015 through ISSUE-0018 records, workflow/status records, relevant security documentation, and current normalization/rule implementation.

The governance validator could not complete because the read-only review environment provided no writable temporary directory; it failed while creating a TemporaryDirectory, before producing a validation result.

evidence: The rule is described as requiring short re-authentication “with no persistent browser session.”
The qualifying algorithm accepts any policy whose persistentBrowser.mode is not "always", so a missing/defaulted value of "" qualifies.
The positive test uses mode "never", but there is no test proving that missing or disabled persistent-browser control fails.
Without an explicit "never" control, the analyzer lacks evidence that persistent browser sessions are prohibited.
findings.remediation: Require persistentBrowser to be enabled with mode exactly "never" (or revise the stated product requirement through an explicit human decision). Add fail cases for missing, disabled, and empty-mode controls while retaining the existing "always" failure case.
findings.title: Admin sign-in-frequency rule can pass without prohibiting persistent browser sessions
findings.verification: Review the amended qualifying algorithm and run analyzer tests demonstrating FAIL for missing/disabled/empty/always persistentBrowser values and PASS only for enabled mode "never" with an otherwise qualifying frequency.

evidence: ISSUE-0018 calls the custom-authentication-strength false-negative limitation “an accepted MVP limitation.”
ROADMAP.md RISK-012 says the same limitation is new, still needs an explicit human treatment decision, and must be accepted before v6 approval.
AGENTS.md prohibits agents from inferring risk acceptance.
findings.remediation: Change ISSUE-0018 to describe the limitation as proposed/pending human acceptance, and make issue start or completion explicitly depend on the recorded RISK-012 decision. Do not label it accepted until the human records that decision.
findings.title: ISSUE-0018 incorrectly records an unaccepted residual risk as accepted
findings.verification: Confirm ROADMAP.md, ISSUE-0018, CURRENT.md, and the eventual decision record consistently distinguish proposed treatment from human acceptance.

evidence: The current rules.RULES list contains 10 rules.
ISSUE-0015 says its implementation must avoid regression of “14 other rules,” although it is the first M4 issue and therefore has only 10 pre-existing rules.
ISSUE-0017 similarly refers to 14 other rules, although sequential implementation would leave 12 pre-existing rules before it.
These counts make the acceptance criteria inaccurate and cannot be verified literally.
findings.remediation: Replace fixed incorrect counts with “all pre-existing rules,” or use the correct issue-specific counts. Keep the milestone-level expectation that the completed rule set totals 14 rules and weight 160.
findings.title: Per-issue regression criteria use impossible existing-rule counts
findings.verification: Count rules.RULES at each issue baseline and confirm each issue criterion refers unambiguously to every rule present before that issue.

evidence: The M4 milestone summary says all four rules read fields currently dropped by normalize_policy.
ISSUE-0015 explicitly requires no graph.py change because includeLocations/excludeLocations are already captured.
Current graph.normalize_policy already retains both location fields.
findings.remediation: Qualify the milestone description: all rules use fields already returned by the existing Graph call, while only ISSUE-0016 through ISSUE-0018 require newly retained normalized fields.
findings.title: M4 summary inaccurately says every proposed rule uses currently dropped fields
findings.verification: Compare the revised roadmap wording with graph.py and each issue's data-contract section.

limitations: The governance validator did not complete because the read-only environment had no usable writable temporary directory; therefore no successful validator evidence is available for this target.

External Microsoft/CIS claims were not independently checked over the network because network access is restricted. ISSUE-0018 appropriately requires fresh source verification at implementation time, but the exact source citation and retrieval evidence remain pending.
No implementation tests were run because this is a roadmap review of unimplemented work; feasibility was assessed against the current source and test contracts.
review.summary: Roadmap v6 is identity-bound correctly and substantially improved, but it still needs three corrections before approval: ISSUE-0017 can pass without an explicit non-persistent-browser control, ISSUE-0018 claims human acceptance that has not occurred, and two issue-level regression criteria use incorrect rule counts. One additional roadmap wording inconsistency is advisory. Governance validation could not complete in the read-only environment.
